newsitem.title: GERMANY: French tax hike not creative accounting - Waigel.
newsitem.headline: French tax hike not creative accounting - Waigel.

text.p: German Finance Minister Theo Waigel said on Monday that French plans to increase taxes could burden the economy, but should not be seen as an attempt to join Europe's single currency through creative accounting.
Waigel told a news conference that his French counterpart Dominique Strauss-Kahn had assured him that France wanted to meet the tough entry criteria in 1998 as well as 1997.

"Only then can sustainable stability be guaranteed," Waigel said. He added that countries would have to be assessed on the basis of final fiscal data for 1997 as well as on their budget plans for 1998.
Asked to comment on France's prospects for joining European economic and monetary union, Waigel said: "I think it would not be good if we gave an assessment of chances."

He added it was up to each country to evaluate its own chances. "I will not participate in speculation here. From a political point of view, it is certain that monetary union without France or Germany makes little sense," he said.

Waigel added that the French government was determined to do what was necessary to meet the criteria, and that it would not let its budget deficit remain at current levels of 3.5, 3.6 or 3.7 percent of GDP.

"France believes it can cut its deficit by 0.4 percentage points through tax measures, and that it has potential for more savings through other measures," Waigel said. He added it was impossible to say exactly what the deficit would be as it depended on growth, the jobs market and tax revenues.
